questions.question: Which element represents self-contained, distributable content like a blog post or news article?
questions.explanation: <article> = independent, reusable content. <section> groups related content (often with a heading).

questions.question: The 'document outline' is built primarily from:
questions.explanation: A logical h1→h6 hierarchy plus landmark/sectioning elements creates an accessible outline for SR users and SEO.

questions.question: What implicit ARIA role does <aside> map to?
Why should you AVOID skipping heading levels (e.g. h1 then h3)?

options.text: It confuses the document outline and assistive-tech navigation
It is invalid HTML that won't render

questions.explanation: Heading levels should reflect structure; skipping levels misleads SR users who navigate by heading.

questions.question: Landmark elements (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>) help users by:

options.text: Letting AT users jump quickly between page regions

questions.explanation: Landmarks create navigable regions; SR users can jump straight to nav/main/complementary content.

questions.question: <time datetime="2025-01-01T09:00Z"> is useful for:

options.text: Providing a machine-readable date/time to parsers and search engines

questions.explanation: The datetime attribute gives a standardized value while the element shows human text — great for events/SEO.

questions.question: A common semantic mistake is:

options.text: Using <div> for everything instead of meaningful landmarks

questions.explanation: Overusing generic divs instead of semantic/landmark elements harms accessibility and SEO.

questions.question: Compared to ARIA, semantic HTML is preferred because it:

options.text: Provides built-in roles/states with less risk and better browser support

questions.explanation: Native semantics are robust and need no extra attributes; ARIA is the fallback for gaps (first rule of ARIA).
